messages:
emma_marketing: Quick ask — we need production-grade, validated benchmark numbers (latency + throughput + unit cost) for the launch blog + webinar next Wed. Can eng/runtime run a sanity check and rerun if needed? Link to draft sheet: https://docs.google.com/sheets/d/1-example (contains the numbers we pulled last week).

sam_runtime: Happy to help. Can you paste which model variant + exact config you want validated (instance type, batch size, seq len, quantization, concurrency)? Also which metrics we should report (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost/M token)?

emma_marketing: Thanks. From the sheet the headline numbers are for "redwood-13b-v1-quant" on A100-80GB: batch_size=8, seq_len=2048, concurrency=4, quant=int8, prefix cache enabled. Metrics: p50, p99, tokens/sec, and an estimated $/1M tokens. We want these numbers checked for 1) methodology errors, 2) rerun to confirm, 3) sanity checks (do results change with cold vs hot cache).

liam_ml: Re: prompts — use prompt_set_v3.json (shared in the sheet). Important: set deterministic sampling for latency runs, and use the same seed for throughput runs so runs are comparable. Watch out for prompt collisions that trigger longer KV cache warmups.

sam_runtime: OK. A few clarifying points:
- Are the published numbers from a single-GPU dedicated machine or our Dedicated pool? (affects routing + batch packing).
- Do we want to include fallback behavior in the number (e.g., serve->fallback to smaller model under load)? For the launch post we typically show baseline numbers for the target variant only.
- Need to confirm whether the original run used continuous batching or explicit static batch.

emma_marketing: They were collected on a single A100-80GB host in our dedicated staging cluster (bench-rt-1). No fallbacks included. Continuous batching was on. We want the same setup so we can say "apples-to-apples."

sam_runtime: Got it. I'll: 1) reproduce the run on bench-rt-1, 2) run cold-cache vs warm-cache, 3) run a deterministic throughput sweep (concurrency 1,2,4,8) and record p50/p95/p99 + tokens/sec. Will also compute cost using the same cost model in the sheet. Expect a quick sanity pass in ~3 hours (subject to queue).

nina_prodops: Heads-up — bench-rt-1 is on a maintenance window at 17:00 UTC today. If you need 3-hour runs, either move to bench-rt-2 or schedule after 20:00 UTC. Also, please use the bench namespace so we don't affect customer pools.

sam_runtime: Thanks @nina_prodops — will use bench-rt-2 and bench namespace. Kicking off now. Command I'm running (for record):
```bash
run_bench --model redwood-13b-v1-quant --host bench-rt-2 --batch 8 --seq 2048 --concurrency 4 --quant int8 --cache prefix --prompts prompt_set_v3.json --deterministic true --out results/1711004823.json
```

ci-bot: Job started: bench-job-1711004823 (owner: sam_runtime). Logs: https://ci.internal/bench-job-1711004823

sam_runtime: First quick pass results: p50=72ms, p95=210ms, p99=370ms, tokens/sec=85 (warm cache). Cold-cache p50=120ms. Cost calc (sheet's cost function): $0.95 / 1M tokens. These are preliminary —I'm re-running the throughput sweep and a 3-run median.

emma_marketing: This is great — two asks: 1) Can you confirm whether continuous batching was enabled (we need to state that explicitly in the methodology blurb)? 2) If p99 is sensitive to concurrency, can you provide a short note we can paste into the blog about variability and the exact test harness (concurrency, warm vs cold)?

sam_runtime: 1) Yes, continuous batching enabled; I'll include the batching window (25ms) and packing heuristics used. 2) Will summarize variability: p99 rises ~1.6x when concurrency goes from 1->8 in this workload; warm-cache vs cold-cache changes p50 by ~1.7x. I'll post a short methodology blurb and attach the raw CSV.

liam_ml: One add — for reproducibility, include the Docker image hash and model artifact SHA we used. Also indicate whether kernel autotuner was active (it was on by default on bench-rt-2).

sam_runtime: Copying that into the report. Docker: redwood/bench:2026-03-20@sha256:abcdef... Model SHA: sha256:12345abcdef. Kernel autotuner: enabled.

emma_marketing: Perfect. Can you also tag any regressions vs last month's run (the sheet has older values)? We need a short line for the PR: "Compared to the Feb run we saw X% lower p50 due to quantization + packing changes."

sam_runtime: Will diff against last run and note changes. If anything looks suspicious I'll flag it for a rerun with identical seeds. ETA final validation summary in ~6 hours. :rocket:

emma_marketing: Awesome — thanks y'all. If the summary is green, we'll lock the blog copy and slides. If you hit any blockers ping me and @liam_ml. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Job completed: bench-job-1711004823 (status: success). Artifacts: https://ci.internal/bench-job-1711004823/artifacts/results.csv

sam_runtime: Final note posted to the sheet + uploaded results.csv. Short publish-ready methodology blurb attached to the sheet. Summary: warm-cache numbers above are stable across 3 runs (median used). No regressions vs Feb except ~6% lower latency due to improved packing. I'll stand by for any follow-ups.

emma_marketing: Perfect — tagging this thread "ready-for-press". Thanks everyone. :tada:
